objective: Run the provisional Gemini 3.8 Flash semantic assessor on the same frozen 16-case rich gold treatment as Claude Sonnet and Opus.
finding: Gemini completed 16/16 cases with 100% required-evidence recall, 97.92% admission accuracy, and 97.78% temporal accuracy. Worthiness-role accuracy was 66.67% and contradiction precision/recall were 37.50%/34.38%. Mean latency was 13.49s. Strict protocol compliance was 6.25% because most responses used fenced JSON normalized by the benchmark.
decision: Do not declare a permanent model winner. Gemini is the strongest candidate for current-admission/temporal gating, while Sonnet remains stronger for semantic role/conflict labeling. Next experiment must measure downstream context-bundle quality rather than label accuracy alone.
next_step: Wire Gemini, Sonnet, and the existing oracle assessor into the evidence admission/context assembly path and compare final bundle recall, noise, conflict preservation, provenance, latency, and downstream answer quality.
